sentences.text:
The Petitioner No.1 to 3 filed petition against Respondent U/sec.12 of Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act by seeking maintenance of Rs. 15,000/-p.m, Rs.5,000/-p.m towards educational expenses, Rs.10,000/- p.m for rent, Rs.30,000/- towards monthly expenses,
Rs.1,00,000/- for litigation expenses and compensation of Rs.5,00,000/-.

entities.text: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
2. The petition averments briefly stated as follows:
The marriage between petitioner No.1 and respondent was solemnized on 05.11.2009 at Siddarudeshrama Kalyana Mantappa, Magadi, after the marriage the petitioner No.1 started to reside with the respondent and his family.
Out of the marriage wedlock they begotten two children.
At the time of the marriage petitioner has given 100 gms of gold, and cash of Rs.75,000/- and spent Rs.6,00,000/- towards marriage expenses.
After the birth of second petitioner, the respondent started harassing the petitioner physically and mentally for dowry and picked up quarrels for the same.
After the advice by panchayatdars the respondent gave an Crl.Misc.No. 218/2016 undertaking that he will not harass the petitioner No.1.
The respondent threatened that he will kill her daughter, assaulted and harrassed the petitioner No.1 to bring dowry.

The respondent used to bring his friends to his house for drinking alcohol and when petitioner No.1 advised not to continue such activities in the house the respondent assaulted the petitioner No.1 with bottle and threatended the petitioner No.1 to 3 with dire consequences.
The entire expenses of the family was born by the father of the petitioner and the respondent used to spend all his money on drinks.

The petitioner No.1 is subjected to physical and mental cruelty by the respondent,
unable to withstand the torture and there were nobody to take care of the petitioner and her children which has become very difficult to lead the life.
Hence the petition.
3. After the serving of notice Respondent appeared before the Court and filed objections.
In the objection the respondent denied all the allegations levelled against him.

The respondent submitted that when the petitioner had been to the delivery of the second child she started to show her true colours and neglected the respondent's family by making unwarranted allegations against respondent and her mother in law.
The petitioner No.1 also scolded for spending medical needs of her mother in law.
The petitioner No.1 choose to quarrel with respondent on filmsy grounds.
The petitioner No.1 is running one Bangle store business which was setup by respondnet and till today the entire income is Crl.Misc.No. 218/2016 taken by her.
The petitioner No.1 in the month of June 2016 willfullly have deserted her husband and residing with her parents.
All the allegation of the petitioner have conveniently been framed with no truth in the same with the children being the witness for the same.
Hence prays to dismiss the petition.

sentences.text: 4. Heard the arguments.

5. On basis of the above mentioned averments the following points do arise for my consideration:
1.
Whether petitioners prove that the respondent has committed domestic violence upon the petitioners?
2. Whether the petitioners prove that they are entitled for the reliefs as sought for?
3. What order?

6. My answer to the above points are as follows:
Point No.1: In the Affirmative Point No.2: Partly in the Affirmative Point No.3: As per final orders for the following:
REASONS 7. Point No.1 : It is the case of the petitioner that she has been physically, mentally assaulted harrassed and subjected to physical and mental cruelty by the respondent Crl.Misc.No. 218/2016 and she is unable to withstand the torture and there were nobody to take care of the petitioner and her children which has become very difficult to lead the life.
Hence petitioner No.1 has filed this petition.
8. On the other hand, the respondent has appeared before this court filed objections but not stepped into witness box to disprove the contentions of the petitioner No.1.
Hence the evidence of PW1 remaind unchallenged.
9. In order to get relief under this petition the petitioner has to prove the domestic relationship and shared house hold.

sentences.text:
As per section 3 of Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005;
Sec.3(a) harms or injuries or endangers the health, safety, life,limb or well-being, whether mental or physical of the aggrieved person or tends to do so and includes causeing physical abuse, sexual abuse, verbal and emotitoinal abuse and economic abuse; or (b) harasses, harms, injuries or endangers the aggrieved person with a view to coerce her or any other person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any dowry or other property or valuable security; or (c) has the effect of threatening the aggrieved person or any person related to her by any conduct mentioned in clause(a) or clause(b); or (d) otherwise injuries or causes harm, whether physical or mental, to the aggrieved person.
Krishna Bhat Chargi Vs. Sarathi Choudary and others(2016) 2 SCC 705, Scheme of 2005 AJ in a beneficial and assertive legislation far more effective protection of constitution rights of women and to ensure that they done become victims of any kind of domestic violence.

sentences.text: On perusal of these depositions it is clear that relationship between the petitioner No.1 and respondent is not in dispute.
It is not in dispute that the petitioner No.1 and respondent stayed together as husband and wife.
Thus the fact of domestic relationship and shared household between the parties are proved.
The petitioner in order to prove her case examined herself as PW1 and marked documents Ex.P1 and P2.
Ex.P1 is the marriage invitation and Ex.P2 is the school fees records.

In the examination in chief affidavit the petitioner reitarated the petition averments and submitted that the respondnet is financially well off and leading happay and luxurious life out of his earnings and he never bothered to provide food, shelter, hospital expenses, education to petitioner No.2 and 3 and presently the entire expenses are being taken care by her father.
The petitioner submitted that she was subjected to physical, mental, economic and emotional abuse by the respondent.
The version of PW1 so as to domestic violence sufferred by her in the hands of respondent remained unchallenged as she was not cross examined.
Nothing is there to disbelieve the version of PW1 so as to domestic violence and the petitioner has utterly proved her case against respondent.
Hence I answer point no.1 in the affirmative.
13. Point No.2: On perusal of evidence of PW1 she was subjected to domestic violence.
In order to protect the petitioner No.1 from future domestic violence it is just and proper to grant protection order.
As per the petitioner averment the petitioners are residing in a rented house.
It is the bounden duty of respondent to provide shelter to the petitioners.
The petitioner sought maintenance of Rs.45,000/-p.m, Rs.5,000/-p.m for rent, Rs.5000/-p.m for educational expenses and compensation of Rs.5,00,000/-.

sentences.text: By considering the income of respondent and standard of living of parties this Court is of a view that the petitioner No.1 is entitled for maintenance of Rs.4,000/-p.m.
There is no convincing evidence to grant compensation as sought for.
Hence I answer Point No 2 partly in the Affairmative.
14. Point No.3:
In view of the discussions made in the point No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass following.
ORDER The petition filed by petitioner U/sec 12 of Protection of Women Domestic Violence Act is hereby partly allowed.
